rationale: PF12296 is the Mp1p/Afmp galactomannoprotein family, whose characterised A. fumigatus members have a signal peptide, a long Ser/Thr-rich O-mannosylated region and a C-terminal GPI attachment signal, and Afmp1p was immunogold-localised to hyphal and conidial cell walls. This entry matches that architecture (SP, GPI, Ser+Thr 0.44, 19 repeat copies, hydrophobic tail 2.1) but its 591 aa length matches neither Afmp1p (284 aa) nor Afmp2p (510 aa), so the family member is not pinned down. It is a wall mannoprotein by architecture, not a demonstrated adhesin; UniProt cell-wall text is unreviewed annotation transfer.
open_questions: Which AFMP paralogue this locus is (BLAST against Afmp1-4), and whether anti-Afmp antibody or a wall-protein extraction assigns the 591 aa product to the wall.

rationale: Signal peptide, hydrophobic C-terminal tail (2.5) and a GPI call with 929 of 980 residues disordered and 7 repeat copies is the generic GPI cell-wall mannoprotein layout. Against it, Ser+Thr is only 0.15, which is low for a heavily O-mannosylated stalk, and there is no Pfam domain, no GO term and no function text, so the GPI claim rests on the protein name plus the predictor. No paper names this locus.
open_questions: Does the C-terminus contain a real omega site (big-PI/NetGPI) and is the protein released by HF-pyridine or beta-1,3-glucanase from the wall fraction?

rationale: PF30910 (agglutinin-like protein middle domain) plus signal peptide, GPI call, hydrophobic tail (2.0) and Ser+Thr 0.37 over 1036 aa is the canonical adhesin layout: N-terminal ligand-binding region, O-glycosylated stalk, GPI anchor. The ALS-middle-domain hit is a profile match in an Aspergillus protein, not an orthology statement, and A. fumigatus has no experimentally characterised ALS-family adhesin that I could retrieve. Repeat coverage is 0.00, so it lacks the tandem-repeat domain that the Candida ALS proteins use for aggregation.
open_questions: Does the N-terminal region fold as a PA14/Ig-like ALS adhesin domain (structure prediction plus HHpred), and does deletion reduce binding to host matrix or epithelium?

rationale: Signal peptide and a hydrophobic C-tail (...SLLVKFLLLVLLIV) preceded by small residues give a credible GPI signal, but the mature protein is about eight tandem 70-aa Cys-rich modules (motif YPQCFNK..CCF..VLYPKPC, 34 Cys in total) followed by a Ser/Thr stalk unusually rich in Asp, Glu and Lys. This matches no adhesin family (no PA14, Flo11, Als or Hyr/Iff head, no Pfam hit) and the charged stalk is not the neutral O-mannosylated stalk of flocculin/ALS mannoproteins. Plausibly a GPI-anchored surface protein of an unknown class (orf19.7836), but it cannot be placed as adhesin-like from the evidence.
open_questions: Profile/structure prediction of the Cys-rich repeat; CGD phenotype and localization data for orf19.7836; SC5314 wall proteomics (trypsin shaving or HF-pyridine release) to test wall incorporation.

rationale: The name Flo11 domain-containing protein is a Google ProtNLM machine prediction and the entry carries no Pfam, PROSITE or InterPro Flo11 match; only about 35 residues separate the signal peptide from a 700-aa Ser/Thr/Pro stalk, far too short for a Flo11A FN3-like domain (about 180 aa), so the Flo11 label is unsupported. Signal peptide, 52 percent Ser/Thr with 11 percent Pro and a hydrophobic C-tail (...FSFLAMIAWVFLM) fit a GPI-anchored mucin-like wall protein without a ligand-binding head. It is not Scf1 (B9J08_001458), Iff4109 or Als4112, which are the characterized C. auris adhesins.
open_questions: Check the gene model for a missing upstream exon (preliminary WGS entry); run HMMER with the Flo11 and PA14 profiles on the full locus; wall proteomics of strain B8441.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal Hyr1-like domain (PF20646), a Thr-rich stalk (Thr 0.17, Ser+Thr 0.29) carrying tandem repeats (8 copies, z 6.7) and a hydrophobic C-terminal tail (2.77) with a positive GPI call is the canonical Hyr/Iff-type GPI cell wall protein architecture. The only literature is family level: C. albicans Hyr1 defines this domain as a GPI wall protein (PMID 8808922) and C. glabrata carries 67 adhesin-like GPI genes in such clusters (PMID 18806209). TrEMBL entry with no functional annotation, so no direct evidence for this locus.
open_questions: Confirm the locus appears in the de Groot 2008 or Xu 2020 GPI-CWP tables and check wall-proteome MS datasets for peptides from this protein.

rationale: Subtelomeric locus with signal peptide, Hyr1-like N-terminal domain, a Thr-rich repeat stalk (12 copies, z 10.1, coverage 0.33) and a strongly hydrophobic C-terminal tail (2.81) with GPI call; this is the Hyr/Iff-type GPI-CWP layout and the narrow rule fires. No paper names the locus; the family evidence is C. albicans Hyr1 (PMID 8808922) and the genome-wide C. glabrata adhesin-like GPI protein catalogs (PMIDs 18806209, 32068314).
open_questions: Wall-proteome MS or an epitope-tagged localization would settle it; check the Xu 2020 corrected repeat structure for this gene.

rationale: Signal peptide plus an N-terminal PA14/GLEYA lectin domain (the Epa/Pwp A-domain fold, PMID 26105055) followed by a long Ser/Pro/Asn-rich disordered region (1085 aa) and a hydrophobic GPI tail (2.19, GPI call positive) is the Epa-like adhesin layout; the subtelomeric chromosome K-left position matches where C. glabrata adhesin-like genes cluster (PMIDs 18806209, 29874814). No paper names the locus, so evidence is family level only.
open_questions: Express the A-domain and test galactoside binding as done for the 17 Epa paralogs; check whether this locus is one of the Pwp genes of de Groot 2008.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal PA14/GLEYA domain, a Gly-rich (0.20) low-complexity stalk with 13 tandem repeats (z 12) and a hydrophobic C-terminus (2.33) with a positive GPI call fit a PA14-type GPI-anchored adhesin of the Epa/Pwp clusters (PMIDs 26105055, 18806209). Only family-level literature; the TrEMBL entry carries no function.
open_questions: Check the corrected gene model in the Xu 2020 assembly (repeat-rich subtelomeric genes were often misassembled) and test A-domain lectin activity.

rationale: Signal peptide, Hyr1-like N-terminal domain, Thr-rich repeats (6 copies, z 10.8, coverage 0.28) and a hydrophobic tail (2.81) with GPI call; all three models and the narrow rule agree, and the architecture is the Hyr/Iff-type GPI-CWP (PMID 8808922 for the domain-defining ortholog; PMID 18806209 for the C. glabrata family). No locus-specific paper.
open_questions: Wall-proteome MS detection or deletion/adhesion assay for this locus.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal PA14 lectin domain, a Ser/Pro-rich stalk and a hydrophobic C-terminus (2.42) that the GPI predictor accepts, at a subtelomeric locus, is the Epa-type adhesin layout (PMID 26105055). I disagree with the lead's membrane concern: the TrEMBL "Transmembrane helix" keyword on a signal-peptide protein with a single C-terminal hydrophobic segment is almost always the GPI attachment signal mis-called as a TM helix, not a true membrane anchor. No locus-specific literature.
open_questions: Verify that the predicted TM segment is the C-terminal 20-25 residues and that an omega site precedes it; if the hydrophobic segment were internal the verdict would change.

rationale: Awp1 was identified directly by tandem MS of isolated C. glabrata cell walls as a covalently bound adhesin-like wall protein (PMID 18806209), and the crystal structure of its A-region shows a parallel right-handed beta-helix plus beta-sandwich, a novel adhesin-like fold (PMID 34962966); the signal peptide, Ser-rich repeat stalk (23 copies) and hydrophobic GPI tail (2.76) complete the picture. Caveat: awp1 deletion did not give an adhesion phenotype in that study and the beta-helix domain bound neither carbohydrate nor Ca2+, so it is a confirmed wall protein with adhesin-like architecture rather than a proven adhesin.
open_questions: Identify the Awp1 ligand or a condition in which awp1 deletion changes adhesion.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal PA14/GLEYA domain, Thr-rich (0.18) body and a hydrophobic GPI tail (2.74) are the Epa-type adhesin architecture (PMID 26105055). The 4336-aa length with almost no detected repeats is suspicious: the CBS138 reference scrambled many repeat-rich GPI-CWP genes and Xu et al. corrected or removed dozens (PMID 32068314), so this gene model may be a misassembly merge; the architecture call does not depend on the length. No locus-specific paper.
open_questions: Compare this locus with the Xu 2020 long-read CBS138 assembly to confirm the gene model and repeat structure before trusting its length or repeat numbers.

rationale: Signal peptide, Hyr1-like N-terminal domain, a Thr-rich (0.18) body and a strongly hydrophobic C-terminal tail (2.82) with a positive GPI call at a chromosome E-left subtelomeric position fit the Hyr/Iff-type GPI-CWP (PMIDs 8808922, 18806209). As for Q6FK94, the UniProt "Transmembrane helix" keyword most likely reflects the GPI signal, so I do not read it as a TM-anchored membrane protein. This is a newer gene model (W0 accession, 2014) with no repeats detected and no literature.
open_questions: Confirm the hydrophobic segment is C-terminal with an omega site; confirm the gene model against the Xu 2020 assembly.

rationale: Signal peptide, Hyr1-like N-terminal domain and then an extraordinary 2100-aa Gly/Ser-rich low-complexity region (Gly 0.32, Ser 0.28) ending in a hydrophobic GPI tail (2.39); C. albicans Hyr1 itself has a Gly/Ser/Asn-rich domain of this kind (PMID 8808922), so the layout is the Hyr ortholog type rather than a repeat-stalk flocculin. No locus-specific paper; the repeat tool finds nothing because the region is low-complexity, not periodic.
open_questions: Wall-proteome detection; check whether the Gly/Ser region is O-mannosylated and whether the gene model is intact in the long-read assembly.

rationale: Signal peptide, Hyr1-like N-terminal domain, a Ser-rich stalk with 45 short tandem repeats (z 6.5) and a hydrophobic tail (2.10) with GPI call, at the chromosome C-left subtelomere next to the EPA6/EPA8 region; this is the Hyr/Iff-type GPI-CWP architecture (PMIDs 8808922, 18806209). One model (gboost 0.16) dissents but the other two and the architecture agree. No locus-specific literature.
open_questions: Wall-proteome MS or tagged localization; check the repeat count against the Xu 2020 assembly.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal PA14 lectin domain, Ser/Pro-rich stalk and hydrophobic GPI tail (2.44) is the Epa adhesin architecture (PMID 26105055), and EPA8 is named directly: its expression was induced by C. albicans germ tubes and it was implicated in C. glabrata adhesion to C. albicans hyphae (PMID 27029023). Direct evidence is genetic/expression rather than wall proteomics, hence medium confidence; the UniProt entry is unreviewed.
open_questions: Wall-proteome detection of Epa8 and a ligand-binding assay of its A-domain would raise this to high.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal PA14 lectin domain, a repeat-rich Cys-containing B region (25 copies, Cys 0.046) and a hydrophobic GPI tail (1.95) match the Epa paralog layout whose A-domains are galactoside-binding lectins (PMID 26105055). EPA10 is named only as a fast-evolving adherence gene in a population-genomics study (PMID 31059831), which is not functional evidence; I could not confirm from the abstract that Epa10 was among the 17 A-domains tested by Diderrich et al.
open_questions: Check the Diderrich 2015 supplement for Epa10 A-domain binding data; wall-proteome detection.

rationale: Signal peptide, Hyr1-like N-terminal domain, Thr-rich (0.15) body and a strongly hydrophobic C-terminal tail (3.02) with GPI call fit the Hyr/Iff-type GPI-CWP (PMIDs 8808922, 18806209); no tandem repeats were detected and the locus is not subtelomeric, so the stalk may be shorter or diverged. No locus-specific literature; TrEMBL entry.
open_questions: Wall-proteome MS detection; inspect the stalk for diverged O-mannosylation repeats.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal PA14 lectin domain, a long Cys-containing repeat B region (37 copies, coverage 0.42) and a hydrophobic GPI tail (1.95) are the Epa paralog layout; the UniProt 3D-structure and calcium keywords are consistent with Epa A-domain crystal structures of the Ca2+-dependent galactoside lectin type (PMID 26105055), though I could not verify Epa9 by name in that abstract and the full text was not retrievable. EPA9 is named only as fast-evolving in a population-genomics study (PMID 31059831).
open_questions: Confirm the PDB entry behind the 3D-structure keyword is an Epa9 A-domain with ligand; wall-proteome detection.

rationale: Paralog of Q6FX23 at the chromosome C-left subtelomere: signal peptide, Hyr1-like N-terminal domain, Ser-rich stalk with 47 short repeats (z 7.1) and a hydrophobic tail (2.10) with GPI call, the Hyr/Iff-type GPI-CWP layout (PMIDs 8808922, 18806209). Only 2 of 3 models call it (gboost 0.036) but the architecture is intact. No locus-specific literature.
open_questions: Wall-proteome MS or tagged localization.

rationale: Signal peptide, Hyr1-like N-terminal domain, Thr-rich (0.15) body and a strongly hydrophobic C-terminal tail (2.99) with GPI call fit the Hyr/Iff-type GPI-CWP (PMIDs 8808922, 18806209); no repeats detected and only 2 of 3 models call it, so it is the weakest of the Hyr-like set here. No locus-specific literature.
open_questions: Wall-proteome MS detection; check the gene model and stalk in the Xu 2020 assembly.

rationale: Awp6 was identified by tandem MS of isolated C. glabrata biofilm cell walls as a novel adhesin-like wall protein with growth-medium-dependent up-regulation (PMID 21769633); the protein has a signal peptide, a Hyr1-like N-terminal domain (PF20646), an Srp1/Tip1-family segment (PF00660), a Ser/Pro-rich stalk and a hydrophobic GPI tail (2.35). The gboost model scores it 0.003, which I disagree with: the wall-proteome evidence is direct. The mapping relies on the UniProt AWP6 gene name for Q6FSJ1.
open_questions: Confirm the Q6FSJ1 locus equals the Awp6 of Kraneveld 2011; adhesion phenotype of an awp6 deletion.

rationale: Signal peptide, GPI call, hydrophobic tail 1.8, Pro 0.22 and 9 tandem repeat copies covering 61 percent of the sequence is the Pro-rich repeat wall-glycoprotein pattern seen in Coccidioides SOWgp, so a surface glycoprotein is a reasonable reading. The seven annotated histidine-triad hairpin repeats (PF28209/PF28210) are not a known adhesin module and could equally indicate a metal-binding surface protein, so the family assignment does not support an adhesin call. No literature names this locus.
open_questions: Expression stage (hypha vs spherule) and whether the repeats bind divalent metals; a wall-fraction proteomic hit would settle surface localisation.

rationale: The SOWgp gene of C. immitis encodes a parasitic-phase spherule outer wall glycoprotein with Pro/Asp-rich tandem repeats whose recombinant form binds laminin, fibronectin and collagen IV, and whose deletion reduced matrix binding and virulence, i.e. direct adhesin evidence. This 324 aa entry with 4 repeat copies, Pro 0.16 and 58 percent repeat coverage matches the described 328 aa four-repeat isolate variant almost exactly, so the isolate-dependent length is expected rather than a mismatch. SOWgp expression is also Ryp1-dependent and spherule-specific, consistent with the parasitic-phase surface antigen.
open_questions: Confirm by direct sequence alignment that CIMG_04613 is the SOWgp ORF of Hung 2002 rather than a paralogue.

rationale: Signal peptide, GPI call, strongly hydrophobic C-terminal tail (2.6), 358 of 372 residues disordered and Ser+Thr 0.30 with Pro 0.19 is a textbook GPI-anchored O-mannosylated wall protein profile with no competing enzymatic or membrane evidence. There are no tandem repeats and no N-terminal ligand-binding domain, so nothing argues specifically for an adhesin rather than a structural mannoprotein. Nothing is known about this locus in the literature.
open_questions: Wall-fraction proteomics of mycelium and spherules, and a big-PI omega-site prediction, would move this to supported or drop it.

rationale: A complete GH18 catalytic domain (PF00704, class III chitinase) makes this a hydrolase, and the Swiss-Prot entry adds a GPI anchor, so it is a wall-associated catalytic enzyme rather than an adhesin. Disruption of the paralogue CTS1 was compensated by elevated CTS2 chitinase activity, which is direct evidence that CTS2 encodes an active chitinase, though CTS2 itself was not disrupted. High Ser+Thr (0.33) and a long disordered run reflect an O-glycosylated linker between the GH18 module and the anchor, which is the usual design of GPI chitinases and does not make it adhesin-like.
open_questions: Whether the catalytic DXXDXDXE motif is intact, and whether a cts2 deletion affects endosporulation or adhesion.

rationale: UniProt locus CPAR2_404790 = CpAls4790: Als N-terminal Ig-like domain (58-305) followed by about 2 kb of Ser/Thr-rich tandem-repeat stalk, signal peptide and hydrophobic C-tail, one of only two C. parapsilosis Als retaining the canonical NT/T/TR/CT organisation. Deletion of CpALS4790 removed more than 60 percent of adhesion to buccal epithelial cells and reduced vaginal colonisation (this locus), and Als6/CPAR2_404790 peptides were recovered from purified CDC317 cell walls. Gene symbol ALS6 is a CGD name; the papers use the locus-derived name.
open_questions: none

rationale: Flo11 (FN3-like) N-terminal domain at 34-252 followed by about 1000 aa of Pro/Ser/Thr-rich flocculin-type-3 repeats (90 copies, 44 percent coverage), signal peptide and C-terminal GPI tail: the canonical Hwp1/Rbt1-type GPI adhesin architecture, and the Flo11 domain is a homotypic/hydrophobic adhesion module. No paper names this locus; the CDC317 wall proteome lists Rbt1 and Ywp1 but not CPAR2_303790.
open_questions: Which Hwp-family member this is in CGD naming (Hwp2-like); proteomic detection in pseudohyphal or high-biofilm isolates

rationale: Hyr/Iff N-terminal domain (11-341) followed by 13 tandem PF15789 cell-wall repeats and a Ser/Thr-rich stalk (0.38), signal peptide and GPI tail, 1671 aa: canonical HYR1/IFF family member in the 806400-806420 tandem cluster of a family that is expanded in C. parapsilosis. Iff proteins are beta-1,6-glucan-linked wall proteins in C. albicans, but the UniProt function text here is transferred (unreviewed) and no paper names this locus.
open_questions: Locus-unique peptides in a wall proteome (Hyr/Iff peptides are largely shared among paralogs)

rationale: 727 aa with signal peptide, GPI call, Ser/Thr 0.37 and Pro 0.14 and six flocculin-type-3 repeat matches, but no Flo11 or any other ligand-binding domain, and about 19 Cys (0.03) is unusual for an Hwp-type stalk and suggests an uncharacterised disulfide-rich N-domain. The name Hyphal wall protein 1 is a propagated/ProtNLM name (the real HWP1 is CPAR2_403520), so I treat it as a stalk-type GPI wall mannoprotein of unknown function.
open_questions: HMM or structure search of the N-terminal 250 aa (Pga/Hwp/Hyr domains); CGD orthology; proteomic detection

rationale: GH18 catalytic domain (21-299) followed by a Ser/Thr-rich flocculin-repeat stalk and GPI tail: the Cht2-type GPI-anchored cell-wall chitinase, and Cht21 peptides were identified in walls of high-biofilm C. parapsilosis isolates. C. albicans Cht2 is cell-bound consistent with GPI anchoring. UniProt cautions that conserved catalytic residues could not be propagated, so the DxxDxDxE motif should be checked; even if degenerate it would be a chitin-binding wall enzyme homolog, not an adhesin.
open_questions: Verify the GH18 DxxDxDxE catalytic motif in the sequence

rationale: Flo11 domain (24-252), Pro-rich (0.17) repeat stalk, signal peptide; the annotated transmembrane helix at 1208-1233 is the C-terminal GPI-attachment hydrophobic tail, so the Membrane/Transmembrane keywords are not evidence against a wall protein. The C. albicans orthologue Hwp1 is a GPI-anchored, beta-glucan-linked hyphal adhesin and transglutaminase substrate; no paper names the C. parapsilosis locus and it was not among proteins identified in CDC317 walls.
open_questions: Whether the N-domain has the Gln/Pro-rich transglutaminase-substrate region; wall proteomics under pseudohyphal conditions

rationale: Flo11 domain (35-262) plus Ser/Thr/Pro repeat stalk, signal peptide and GPI tail. Rbt1 peptides were recovered from purified CDC317 walls and were strongly increased in high-biofilm isolates; a C. parapsilosis RBT1 ortholog knockout reduces biofilm formation and its expression is Bcr1-dependent, and the C. albicans Rbt1 Flo11 domain mediates adhesion to polystyrene.
open_questions: Confirm the RBT1 ortholog deleted in 19151323 is CPAR2_403510 (CGD gene-name mapping)

rationale: 1158 aa with signal peptide, GPI call, Ser/Thr 0.36 and about 780 aa of low-complexity/Gly stalk but no Pfam domain; the name Flo11 domain-containing is a ProtNLM name with no Flo11 hit. It sits next to HYR31 (CPAR2_600430) so it may be a tandem Hyr/Iff-family paralog with a lost or diverged N-domain, but nothing beyond the stalk-plus-GPI profile supports a wall adhesin.
open_questions: HMM/structure search of residues 21-175 for a Hyr or Flo11 fold; proteomic detection

rationale: PGA domain (34-78) followed by a Ser/Thr/Pro-rich low-complexity stalk, signal peptide and GPI tail, 361 aa: the small PGA-domain GPI protein family (Pga13/26/30/31/48 type), which are wall-structural GPI mannoproteins rather than adhesins. C. albicans Pga26 is a small GPI wall protein required for wall integrity, and Pga30 was found in CDC317 walls, but no paper maps this locus.
open_questions: Which Pga this locus corresponds to in CGD; whether it is the Pga30 identified in the wall proteome

rationale: GH18 catalytic domain (22-309) followed by a Ser/Thr-rich flocculin-repeat stalk and GPI tail, 808 aa: a second Cht2-type GPI-anchored wall chitinase, and Cht22 peptides were identified in biofilm walls of high-biofilm isolates. C. albicans Cht2 is cell-bound consistent with GPI anchoring. As for CHT21, UniProt could not propagate catalytic residues, so the DxxDxDxE motif should be checked.
open_questions: Verify the GH18 catalytic motif

rationale: Hyr/Iff N-terminal domain followed by a 2 kb Ser/Thr-rich stalk (0.34), signal peptide and GPI tail, 2273 aa, in the 806400-806420 Hyr/Iff tandem cluster of a family expanded in C. parapsilosis. Architecture matches C. albicans Hyr1 (GPI, large Ser/Thr domain) and Iff proteins that are beta-1,6-glucan-linked; no paper names this locus.
open_questions: Locus-unique wall-proteome peptides

rationale: 522 aa with signal peptide, GPI tail, Ser/Thr 0.32 and flocculin-type-3 repeats (Hwp-like family). Ywp1 (by CGD gene name) is a core CDC317 wall protein found in all four planktonic conditions and most abundant in low-biofilm strains; the C. albicans orthologue is a GPI-anchored, Kex2-processed wall glycoprotein that is anti-adhesive and decreased in hyphae. So it is a wall-anchored Hwp-family GPI protein, but functionally anti-adhesive rather than an adhesin.
open_questions: Confirm CPAR2_806670 is the Ywp1 of the proteome; check for the conserved RRR...KR Kex2 propeptide site

rationale: Hyr/Iff N-terminal domain (12-346), PT repeats and an about 800 aa Ser/Thr/Gly stalk, signal peptide and GPI tail, 1429 aa. Hyr31 was identified only in walls of high-biofilm biofilm-grown isolates, but the authors note most of its peptides are shared with other Iff/Hyr members, so the locus assignment is weaker than for Als proteins.
open_questions: Locus-unique peptides; whether expression is biofilm-linked

rationale: UniProt locus CPAR2_404780 = CpAls4780: Als N-domain (58-306) with Ser/Thr low-complexity and Gly-rich stalk, signal peptide and GPI tail, retaining the canonical Als NT/T/TR/CT organisation. The protein purified from the cell wall binds human epithelial and endothelial cells, fibronectin and vitronectin; the single edited strain had no adhesion defect but the CpALS4770/4780 double mutant was hyper-adhesive and both mutants had reduced vaginal colonisation; Als11 peptides were increased in high-biofilm walls.
open_questions: none

rationale: 889 aa with signal peptide, GPI call, Ser/Thr 0.37 and Cys 0.01; the only Pfam hit is DUF3246 (a serine-rich mucin-like fungal family), with long low-complexity, acidic and Gly stretches and no Hyr N-domain despite the protein name. A mucin-like Ser/Thr stalk plus GPI fits a wall mannoprotein but there is no ligand-binding domain and no literature.
open_questions: Fold search of the N-terminal 50 aa; identity of the C. albicans DUF3246 ortholog; proteomic detection

rationale: UniProt locus CPAR2_500660 is the chromosome-5 ALS gene called CpALS0660 in the full text of 32545584 (CpAls5600 in its abstract): Als N-domain (58-306), Ser/Thr low-complexity and Gly-rich stalk without canonical tandem repeats, signal peptide and GPI tail. The null mutant showed no defect in adhesion to buccal epithelial cells but significantly reduced vaginal colonisation, so direct evidence is for a wall-anchored virulence Als rather than for adhesion per se; not detected by name in the CDC317 wall proteome.
open_questions: Adhesion to other ligands (ECM, endothelial cells); wall-proteome detection

rationale: UniProt locus CPAR2_404770 = CpAls4770: Als N-domain (58-305), Ser/Thr low-complexity stalk, signal peptide and GPI tail. The CpALS4770-edited strain showed reduced biofilm formation and reduced adhesion to buccal epithelial cells and reduced vaginal colonisation (this locus); the CGD name ALS3 does not imply orthology with C. albicans Als3 and not detected by name in CDC317 walls.
open_questions: none

rationale: 261 aa with signal peptide and GPI call, but the mature region (28-247) is disordered with an acidic stretch (80-188) and a Gly stretch (192-228), Pro 0, Cys 0 and Ser/Thr only 0.28; the sole InterPro hit (Toxoplasma dense-granule protein Gra6) is a spurious low-complexity match. Without an O-mannosylated Ser/Thr stalk or any domain this could equally be a small GPI-anchored membrane protein, and all three models call it negative, which I agree with.
open_questions: GPI omega-site prediction, AlphaFold model, expression data

rationale: Hyr/Iff N-terminal domain (11-341), signal peptide and GPI tail, 1714 aa, in the 806400-806420 Hyr/Iff tandem cluster. The stalk is Gly-rich repeat (32 Gly-rich stretches, Ser/Thr only 0.15) rather than the usual Ser/Thr stalk, which resembles the Gly/Ser/Asn-rich second domain of C. albicans Hyr1, so still family-consistent but with less O-mannosylation potential; no paper names this locus.
open_questions: Locus-unique peptides; whether the Gly-rich stalk is O-glycosylated

rationale: ZIP-family (zinc/iron permease, PF02535) multi-pass membrane protein with eight annotated transmembrane helices (321-614); the pipeline GPI call is the last TM helix, not an omega-site tail. The about 300 aa N-terminal extracellular region (PbH1 repeat hits) is unusual but does not change the transporter topology; fungal ZIP proteins (Zrt1/Zrt2) are plasma-membrane zinc uptake transporters.
open_questions: none

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal PA14/GLEYA lectin domain (residues 80-236), 14 Flocculin PF00624 repeats forming a Thr-rich stalk and a hydrophobic C-tail (...ASAPLILALLAFL) reproduce the complete Flo1/Flo5/Flo9 architecture, in which the PA14 domain is the calcium-dependent carbohydrate-binding head. No paper concerns this locus; K. marxianus papers only show that heterologous S. cerevisiae FLO genes confer flocculation in this host and that flocculation gene families are expanded in K. marxianus. The gene name FLO1 versus protein name FLO9 is an annotation inconsistency within one family, not a biological conflict.
open_questions: Flocculation assay of a FIM1 deletion or overexpression strain; mannose inhibition to show Flo1-type lectin specificity.

rationale: Signal peptide, 63 percent Ser/Thr with a 500-aa low-complexity stalk and a hydrophobic C-tail (...LEYLTALAFGLLSLL) with upstream small residues are the hallmarks of a GPI-anchored O-mannosylated wall mannoprotein. The only non-stalk region is about 45 N-terminal residues containing a CxxC pair, so there is no ligand-binding domain and no adhesin family assignment. Fits a Sed1/Cwp-like GPI mannoprotein rather than an ALS/Flo-type adhesin.
open_questions: HMMER against Flo11/PA14/Als profiles; wall proteomics of FIM1; check whether the gene model lacks an N-terminal exon.

rationale: Signal peptide, a PROSITE-confirmed Flo11 domain (residues 50-229), a 900-aa Ser/Thr/Pro stalk (19 percent Pro) and a hydrophobic C-tail (...FTFLSSILAALFLL) reproduce the S. cerevisiae Flo11/Muc1 architecture, whose FN3-like Flo11A head mediates homophilic and plastic adhesion. MUC1 and FLO11 are the two names of the same S. cerevisiae gene, so the name difference is not a conflict, although three FIM1 paralogs share the name. Perpetuini 2019 measured FLO11 ortholog expression in biofilm-forming K. marxianus dairy strains but did not resolve which paralog.
open_questions: Determine which of the three Flo11 paralogs is expressed in FIM1; deletion and biofilm/mat assay.

rationale: Signal peptide, four Flocculin type 3 repeats (PF13928, the repeat found near the C-terminus of S. cerevisiae Flo9), a 52 percent Ser/Thr stalk and a hydrophobic C-tail (...WSLAPVFYLFF) describe a flocculin-type GPI wall protein. The 95-aa region between the signal peptide and the stalk is too short for a PA14 lectin head, so this is a stalk-type Flo-like protein with no identified binding domain, possibly a truncated gene model. The GPI-anchor, membrane and glycoprotein keywords are ARBA automatic annotation, not experiments.
open_questions: Inspect the genome upstream for a PA14-encoding exon; wall proteomics; flocculation assay.

rationale: Signal peptide, about eight tandem 45-aa Thr/Ile/Val-rich repeats (TTEIDTTTELIPIPVTTTMTFTENGTTRVITTT) followed by paired-Cys CGGSPC modules, and a hydrophobic C-tail (...ILLLVSTLISTMFFF) resemble the Thr-rich stalk repeats of Flo1/Flo9-type flocculins. No N-terminal lectin domain is present (repeats begin near residue 60), so it is a GPI-anchored flocculin-like stalk protein whose adhesive function cannot be judged.
open_questions: Check for a missing N-terminal exon; wall proteomics; adhesion assay.

rationale: Signal peptide, PROSITE-confirmed Flo11 domain (residues 30-206), a 650-aa Ser/Thr/Pro stalk and a hydrophobic C-tail (...FISTVLPLVLAAFML) reproduce the Flo11/Muc1 adhesin architecture whose FN3-like head mediates homophilic and surface adhesion. MUC1/FLO11 are synonyms in S. cerevisiae; the name is shared by three FIM1 paralogs. No paper addresses this locus; Perpetuini 2019 reports FLO11 ortholog expression in adhesive K. marxianus strains at the family level.
open_questions: Paralog-specific expression and deletion assays.

rationale: Signal peptide, an Agglutinin-like N-terminal domain (Candida_ALS_N PF11766, residues 54-302; the Ig-like peptide-binding head shared by C. albicans Als proteins and S. cerevisiae alpha-agglutinin Sag1), a 48 percent Ser/Thr stalk and a hydrophobic C-tail (...AIVSIFLSYLAM) give the complete Als/agglutinin GPI-adhesin architecture. The cell adhesion, cell wall and hyphal GO annotations are ARBA transfers from Candida Als entries, not data on this protein. The lead's low confidence underestimates how diagnostic the ALS N-domain is; the family function is well established.
open_questions: Mating agglutination or peptide-binding assay for the K. marxianus protein; confirm it is the alpha-agglutinin ortholog rather than an Als-like paralog.

rationale: The plant name arabinogalactan protein 19 is a transferred mis-annotation triggered by a collagen-like Gly-Pro repeat (PF01391). Signal peptide and a hydrophobic C-tail (...NIVGAGLAVVGAMLL) support a GPI-anchored surface protein, but the 22 percent Pro, Gly-rich, 7-Cys body with only 26 percent Ser/Thr is not the O-mannosylated Ser/Thr stalk of flocculin/ALS mannoproteins and matches no fungal wall family. Cannot be placed from the evidence.
open_questions: Orthology search in Kluyveromyces and Saccharomyces; wall proteomics; HMMER against fungal GPI protein families.

rationale: UniProt lacks the Signal keyword, but the N-terminus (MRLLNVANKVFGTLAIIQGITSA) is a credible signal peptide; a PROSITE-confirmed Flo11 domain (residues 51-230), a 600-aa Ser/Thr/Pro stalk and a hydrophobic C-tail (...FTLLSSFLAAMLLI) complete the Flo11/Muc1 adhesin architecture. MUC1/FLO11 are synonyms; the name is shared by three FIM1 paralogs. Family-level only: no paper addresses this locus.
open_questions: Confirm the signal peptide with SignalP 6; paralog-specific expression and deletion assays.

rationale: Signal peptide, GPI call, hydrophobic tail 2.4, 238 of 244 residues disordered and 68 percent tandem-repeat coverage fit a small repetitive GPI wall mannoprotein. The name proteophosphoglycan ppg4 is transferred from Leishmania, an organism with no fungal cell wall, so it carries no information about function here and should be ignored. Only one of three models called it, and no literature exists for R. toruloides surface proteins of this kind.
open_questions: Is the repeat Ser/Thr-rich and O-mannosylated (mass spectrometry of the wall fraction of R. toruloides), and is there an omega site?

rationale: Signal peptide and a fully disordered Ser/Thr-rich (0.37) sequence are consistent with a secreted O-glycosylated protein, but the C-terminal tail hydrophobicity is negative (-0.6) and there is no GPI call, so it cannot be a GPI-anchored wall protein. Without a GPI anchor, a repeat domain, a Pfam hit or any functional annotation, the protein could equally be a secreted glycopeptide unrelated to the wall. The three models calling it most likely respond to disorder and Ser/Thr content alone.
open_questions: Secretome versus wall-fraction proteomics would distinguish a released protein from a non-covalently wall-bound one.

rationale: Same reasoning as the other Afum extracellular Thr-rich entry: signal peptide and a 606-residue disordered region, but no GPI, negative tail hydrophobicity (-0.3), no repeats and no domain. Ser+Thr 0.26 with Pro 0.16 is consistent with an O-mannosylated secreted protein but does not distinguish wall anchoring from simple secretion. The putative name is an annotation guess, not evidence.
open_questions: Is the protein recovered from alkali- or glucanase-extracted wall fractions, and does it carry an omega site?

rationale: A GH16 catalytic module with a GPI anchor and Swiss-Prot annotation as an endo-1,3(4)-beta-glucanase makes this a wall-remodelling transglycosylase/hydrolase, the classic counter-example to an adhesin. Low repeat content (0.00), moderate Ser+Thr (0.25) and no ligand-binding N-terminal domain give no adhesin signal, and all three models correctly declined to call it. Its wall association is enzymatic, not adhesive.
open_questions: Whether the GH16 ExDxxE catalytic motif is intact and whether the enzyme is a Bgt/Crh-type transglycosylase rather than a hydrolase.

rationale: Signal peptide but no hydrophobic C-tail (...PAKSTTLSN) and no internal TM helix, so it is neither GPI- nor membrane-anchored. A 290-aa N-terminal Cys-rich region (20 Cys) that is shared with the paralog orf19.11471 is followed by GGGNN repeats and acidic TEPTDPT Thr-Pro repeats; this yeast-specific family (orf19.9985) has no Pfam match and no adhesin architecture. A secreted or alkali-labile wall protein is possible but cannot be judged.
open_questions: CGD annotation and localization for orf19.9985; secretome or wall proteomics; structure prediction of the Cys-rich domain.

rationale: Signal peptide but no hydrophobic C-tail (...STLATTVVK) and no internal TM helix, so not GPI- or membrane-anchored. The N-terminal Cys-rich region is paralogous to orf19.9985 (same CxxxF/CP motifs), followed by Thr-rich and DKP-repeat acidic segments; no Pfam match and no adhesin architecture. A secreted protein of a yeast-specific family; function cannot be judged.
open_questions: CGD annotation for orf19.11471; secretome proteomics; structure prediction.

rationale: A glycoside hydrolase family 17 catalytic domain (residues 247-500) with the GLYCOSYL_HYDROL_F17 PROSITE active-site signature, and no GPI tail (...YFGVIQLFQ), make it a secreted or alkali-linked beta-1,3-glucanase/transglycosylase of the Scw4/Scw10/Scw11 class. Klis 2015 names SCW11 as a periodically expressed beta-1,3-glucan-modifying enzyme whose secretion tracks cell separation, and S. cerevisiae Scw4/Scw10 are covalently wall-bound GH17 enzymes. The N-terminal Thr/Gln-rich region is a stalk, not an adhesin head.
open_questions: None needed for the verdict; glucanase or transglycosylase activity assay would refine the catalytic mode.

rationale: Signal peptide, two Flocculin type 3 repeats (PF13928), 35 percent Ser/Thr and a hydrophobic C-tail (...FLGGLSLLLAIL) fit a flocculin-type GPI wall protein, but at 332 aa with no PA14/GLEYA head it is a stalk-only fragment-like protein, possibly a truncated gene model in a preliminary WGS entry. Alvarado 2024 reports Flo5-like flocculins among C. auris GPI proteins without naming this locus.
open_questions: Inspect the genome neighbourhood for an upstream exon or adjacent flocculin fragment; adhesion assay.

rationale: The N-terminus (MLWILYIAAAMAA) is a credible signal peptide although UniProt lacks the keyword; a Thr/Ala/Gly/Pro-rich low-complexity body (28 percent Thr) and a hydrophobic C-tail (...LSWLASGLFLLGYAI) fit a small GPI-anchored mannoprotein of the Cwp/Pga type. No ligand-binding domain and no family, so adhesin function is not indicated; the models score it low, but the biochemical features of a GPI wall protein are present.
open_questions: Confirm the signal peptide; wall proteomics; orthology search.

rationale: Signal peptide and a hydrophobic C-tail (...TVLVGVIAALTLGLHSL) support GPI anchoring, but the body is Asn/Gly/Thr/Ala-rich (14 percent Asn, no Cys) rather than a Ser/Thr O-mannosylation stalk and matches no family. Could be one of the C. auris-specific GPI proteins or a mis-modelled ORF; cannot be judged.
open_questions: Check the gene model; wall proteomics; orthology search across Candidozyma.

rationale: Signal peptide, Hyr1-like N-terminal domain, Thr-rich repeats (7 copies, z 8.0, coverage 0.29) and a hydrophobic tail (2.17) with GPI call at a chromosome K-right subtelomeric position; all three models call it and the layout is the Hyr/Iff-type GPI-CWP (PMIDs 8808922, 18806209). No locus-specific literature; TrEMBL entry.
open_questions: Wall-proteome MS detection or deletion/adhesion assay.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal PA14/GLEYA lectin domain and a hydrophobic GPI tail (2.49) make a PA14-type GPI-CWP, the Pwp (PA14-containing wall protein) class named in the C. glabrata adhesin inventory (PMID 18806209; fold per PMID 26105055). PWP5 appears by name only as an "adhesin gene" with SNPs in a resistance-marker study (PMID 28344162), which is not functional evidence; the stalk is short on disorder (94) and repeat-free, so it may be a compact PA14 wall protein rather than a long-stalk adhesin.
open_questions: A-domain ligand-binding assay and wall-proteome detection.

rationale: Signal peptide and N-terminal PA14/GLEYA domain fit the Epa/Pwp fold (PMID 26105055), but the C-terminus is not hydrophobic (0.45) and the GPI call is negative, so as modelled this protein cannot be covalently wall-anchored through GPI-beta-1,6-glucan. The locus sits in the chromosome I-right subtelomeric adhesin cluster where the CBS138 reference has many scrambled repeat-rich gene models (PMID 32068314), so a truncated or misassembled model is the most likely explanation; otherwise it would be a secreted or alkali-sensitive-linked PA14 protein. No locus-specific literature.
open_questions: Check the gene end in the Xu 2020 long-read assembly for a restored GPI signal; if the model is correct, test whether the protein is secreted or wall-bound.

rationale: The only functional annotation is GO actin filament binding and cortical actin cytoskeleton organisation with cytoplasm/cytoskeleton components, which places it inside the cell. There is no GPI call, tail hydrophobicity is 0.7 and Pro is 0.20 over a 906-residue disordered run, a composition typical of large intracellular scaffolding proteins as much as of wall proteins. The signal-peptide keyword conflicts with the GO terms; the GO terms are themselves electronic transfers, so confidence is low in either direction.
open_questions: Re-run SignalP and check whether the predicted N-terminus is a genuine signal peptide or a mis-called first exon; localisation by tagging would settle it.

rationale: For a 212 aa protein with a signal peptide, a GPI call and a strongly hydrophobic C-terminal tail (2.6), the single UniProt transmembrane helix is almost certainly the GPI omega-site hydrophobic stretch mis-annotated by a TM predictor, so I disagree with the Transmembrane keyword rather than treat it as a membrane protein. The remaining features, a 178-residue disordered Ser/Pro-rich region between signal peptide and anchor, fit a small GPI wall mannoprotein. The GPI claim nevertheless rests on the protein name and prediction only, with no domain, GO term or paper.
open_questions: Compare the C-terminal 30 residues against an omega-site model (big-PI/NetGPI); a positive omega site would resolve the TM versus GPI conflict.

rationale: The name says serine-threonine rich but the measured Ser+Thr fraction is only 0.11, below the proteome average, so the name is wrong or refers to a small region and cannot be used as evidence. There is no GPI call, tail hydrophobicity is 0.7, repeat coverage is 0.09 and there is no domain, GO term or literature. A 422-residue disordered secreted protein with these numbers has no feature that points to a wall adhesin.
open_questions: Recompute composition per segment to see if a short Ser/Thr block exists, and check the secretome for the protein.

rationale: The name claims an enzyme but no Pfam, InterPro domain, GO term or catalytic motif is annotated, so neither the enzyme call nor a wall call can be supported. Signal peptide plus a GPI call and a modest hydrophobic tail (1.5) with Ser+Thr 0.29 and 8 short repeat copies is weakly consistent with a small surface glycoprotein, but the longest disordered run is only 94 residues, too short for a mannoprotein stalk. I decline to follow the pipeline towards either a wall protein or an enzyme.
open_questions: A domain search (HHpred/structure prediction) to test the aldehyde-forming enzyme claim, and a GPI omega-site check.

rationale: Signal peptide, GPI call, hydrophobic tail 2.0, Ser+Thr 0.40 and a 501-residue disordered run in a 631 aa protein is the composition of a GPI-anchored O-mannosylated wall protein, and in Cryptococcus the mannoprotein class is well represented in the wall and in extracellular vesicles. As with the other Cryptococcus entries, the Transmembrane keyword most likely reflects the GPI tail rather than a real membrane span. No Pfam domain, no GO term and no paper names this locus, and no model called it, so this is architecture only.
open_questions: Wall or extracellular-vesicle proteomics of H99 and an omega-site prediction; a deletion phenotype in adhesion assays would be decisive.

rationale: The GPI call and a hydrophobic tail (2.6) point to an anchored surface protein, but Ser+Thr is only 0.15 and Pro 0.15, repeat coverage 0.00 and the longest disordered run is 200 of 428 residues, so there is no O-mannosylated stalk of the flocculin/mannoprotein type. No domain, GO term, function text or literature exists, and all three models declined to call it. The evidence is too thin to choose between a wall protein, a membrane protein and something else.
open_questions: Resolve GPI versus transmembrane by omega-site prediction and hydropathy of the tail; then look for the protein in wall fractions.

rationale: 257 aa with signal peptide, GPI tail, Ser/Thr 0.30 and flocculin-type-3 repeats. The C. albicans orthologue Pga62 is a short N- and O-glycosylated GPI protein located in the cell wall and required for wall integrity and caspofungin response, not an adhesin; the name Hyphal wall protein 1 is a ProtNLM artefact. Not detected in the CDC317 wall proteome (Pga59 was).
open_questions: Proteomic detection; whether CPAR2_403180 is the true Pga62 ortholog in CGD

rationale: CFEM domain (34-145) with four disulfides and a heme axial ligand at residue 80, followed by about 770 aa of acidic/low-complexity regions with PGA60 trefoil-like repeat hits, signal peptide and GPI call: the long Csa1-type CFEM hemophore architecture, i.e. a GPI wall mannoprotein of the heme-acquisition class rather than an adhesin. C. parapsilosis has seven CFEM genes, of which CFEM2/3/6 (not CFEM5) were shown to act in heme-iron acquisition, and C. albicans Csa1/Rbt5/Pga7/Pga10 are GPI wall proteins whose CFEM domains bind heme; Csa1 was found in high-biofilm walls but is not mapped to this locus.
open_questions: Map CFEM1-7 of Ding 2011 to CPAR2 loci; GPI omega-site versus secretion (UniProt says Secreted only)

rationale: 1307 aa with Ser/Thr 0.37 and no Cys; UniProt annotates only an N-terminal hydrophobic segment (7-25) as a transmembrane helix, which by position and length is a signal peptide (pipeline SP=1), and the pipeline finds a C-terminal GPI tail, so the Membrane/Transmembrane keywords do not indicate a membrane protein. The name Flo11 domain-containing is a ProtNLM name with no Flo11 hit; the stalk-only Ser/Thr-rich GPI profile fits a wall mannoprotein but there is no domain and no literature.
open_questions: SignalP/NetGPI check; HMM search of the N-terminal 300 aa for Hyr/Flo11/Als folds; proteomic detection

rationale: Signal peptide and the most hydrophobic C-tail in the batch (...MTIILTIACVVMLPLVL) give a strong GPI signal; the 22 percent Thr body with scattered TTTT stretches, only two Cys and no Pfam hit fits a GPI-anchored Thr-rich mannoprotein of the Sed1/Ccw type. No repeats or binding domain, so not an adhesin by architecture.
open_questions: Wall proteomics of FIM1; orthology search.

rationale: Signal peptide, Kex2 cleavage site, eight PIR repeats (PF00399) and the Cys-containing PIR1-like C-terminal domain with no GPI tail (...AIDLVSC) define a Pir-family wall mannoprotein, which is linked to beta-1,3-glucan through its repeats by an alkali-labile ester bond rather than a GPI anchor; all four S. cerevisiae Pir proteins were found covalently in the wall. It is a structural wall mannoprotein, not an adhesin, and no study addresses the K. marxianus gene. The HSP150 versus PIR1 name difference is within the family.
open_questions: Alkali (NaOH) extraction of FIM1 walls with mass spectrometry would confirm wall incorporation.

rationale: PF21671 identifies this as a CPL1-like protein; in C. neoformans the Cpl1 ortholog is a small secreted cysteine-rich protein that was shown by specific antibody and immunostaining to sit on the cell surface, and that acts as a secreted effector driving macrophage polarisation. That makes a surface-associated protein plausible, but the Rhodotorula protein has no GPI call, tail hydrophobicity 1.5 and only Cys 0.04 with no Ser/Thr stalk or repeats, so it is not of the GPI flocculin/ALS/mannoprotein type. The evidence here is orthology to a different species, not data on this protein.
open_questions: Does R. toruloides Cpl1-like protein localise to the wall or the supernatant, and is the CPL1 cysteine-rich fold intact in this 553 aa protein?

rationale: Signal peptide, GPI call, Ser+Thr 0.27 and a 332-residue disordered region fit a GPI wall mannoprotein, but the tail hydrophobicity is only 1.1, weaker than the usual omega-site tail, and repeat coverage is 0.00. The name proteophosphoglycan 5 is transferred from a trypanosomatid annotation and carries no weight for a basidiomycete yeast. No model called it and no literature exists, so this is a weak architecture-only call.
open_questions: A proper omega-site prediction plus wall-fraction proteomics of R. toruloides.

rationale: PF01764 is an AB-hydrolase lipase domain and the Swiss-Prot entry describes a single-pass type II membrane protein of the multivesicular body and prevacuolar compartment that lyses autophagic bodies in the vacuolar lumen, i.e. an intracellular lipase. The signal-anchor, not a cleaved signal peptide, is what the pipeline read as a secretion signal, and the moderate Ser/Thr content is incidental. Nothing about this protein is wall-related; the pipeline lead is simply wrong here, and only one of three models called it.
open_questions: None needed for the wall question; an atg15 deletion would test autophagy function, not wall localisation.

rationale: PF10342 is the Kre9/Knh1 N-terminal domain; Kre9 and Knh1 are cell-wall glycoproteins required for beta-1,6-glucan synthesis in S. cerevisiae and C. glabrata, where their loss cuts beta-1,6-glucan by half and causes severe wall defects. Together with the signal peptide, GPI call, hydrophobic tail (2.4) and Ser+Thr 0.36, this is a genuine cell-wall glycoprotein, but of the wall-assembly class rather than an adhesin, and Kre9/Knh1 have no assigned catalytic activity so I do not call it an enzyme. The family evidence is from yeasts, not from this A. fumigatus gene.
open_questions: Whether deletion in A. fumigatus reduces beta-1,6-glucan or wall integrity, which would confirm the Kre9 role over an adhesin role.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal WSC domain, Ser/Thr-rich stalk, an internal hydrophobic helix at about residues 326-349 (FTAVGIVVVGIVGAMLYCCCC) and a 140-aa cytoplasmic tail is the type I membrane architecture of Wsc proteins; the hydrophilic C-terminus (...KLKITNPE) excludes a GPI anchor, and UniProt simply missed the TM. S. cerevisiae Wsc4 (YHL028W, YHC8) is an ER membrane protein acting in protein translocation, and the other Wsc proteins are plasma membrane sensors; neither is a wall-anchored adhesin.
open_questions: Confirm orthology of C. albicans WSC4 to YHL028W versus WSC1-3 and its localization; Phobius/TMHMM on the sequence.

rationale: A credible signal peptide (MKFTKVITAACIASSVESA) is followed by CDTP-x-P repeats, a GGNN block and about 110 residues of DNDSDNDS/DDDC acidic repeats; there is no hydrophobic C-tail (...SDDDC), no TM helix and only 22 percent Ser/Thr. This is a small secreted acidic protein, and nothing links it to wall anchoring or adhesion (orf19.7167).
open_questions: CGD annotation; secretome proteomics; check whether the ORF is dubious.

rationale: KRE1 family (PF17056), signal peptide and a hydrophobic C-tail (...AGIVGWAAIALGYLL); S. cerevisiae Kre1 is a GPI-anchored cell-surface O-glycoprotein with a structural role in beta-1,6-glucan assembly, and InterPro places C. albicans Pga1 (adhesion and biofilm phenotypes) in the same family. At 119 aa it is much shorter than Kre1 (313 aa), so the gene model may be truncated. A GPI wall protein by family, not an adhesin by architecture.
open_questions: Check the gene model length; map to Kre1 versus Pga1 orthology; wall proteomics.

rationale: Signal peptide, WSC domain (residues 16-103), Ser/Thr stalk, a strong Phobius and Kyte-Doolittle TM helix at residues 213-238 and a 100-aa cytoplasmic tail (...DYSRKILAVANP) make this a type I membrane WSC sensor-type protein, not a GPI wall protein. The pipeline flags it only by signal peptide; the TM anchor rules out the flocculin/ALS/GPI-mannoprotein class.
open_questions: Localization; none needed for the class call.

rationale: Signal peptide, N-terminal PA14/GLEYA lectin domain and a hydrophobic C-terminal tail (2.46) with positive GPI call give the Epa-type adhesin layout (PMID 26105055) at a chromosome L-right subtelomeric position (PMID 18806209); the body shows almost no disorder (14) or detected repeats, so the stalk is either compact or built of diverged repeats the tool missed. Only 2 of 3 models call it; no locus-specific literature.
open_questions: A-domain lectin assay; confirm repeat structure and gene model in the Xu 2020 assembly.

rationale: A 294-aa Ser-rich (0.32) protein with signal peptide and a UniProt GPI-CWP annotation transferred by similarity from S. cerevisiae Dse2, an Ace2-dependent daughter-cell-specific gene whose products act in degrading the septum for cell separation (PMIDs 11747810, 14709718); it has no PA14, Hyr, Flo11 or repeat stalk and no catalytic domain is assigned, so it is at most a small GPI-mannoprotein of the separation program, not an adhesin-like protein, and all three models score it low (0.35, 0.04, 0.006), which I agree with. The pipeline C-tail hydrophobicity (-0.03) contradicts its own GPI call, so even the GPI anchoring is not confirmed for this ortholog. No C. glabrata paper exists.
open_questions: Inspect the CBS138 C-terminus for an omega site and hydrophobic tail; if the DSE2/EGT2 family is ever shown to have glucanase activity the verdict would move to enzyme.

rationale: The only annotation is PF28404, described as a Prp6 CRoW domain; Prp6 in yeasts is a nuclear spliceosomal protein, so the name and the predicted signal peptide plus GPI anchor contradict each other and neither can be trusted. Composition is unremarkable for a wall protein (Ser+Thr 0.17, no repeats, 104-residue disordered run in 214 aa), and no model called it. My PubMed search for this domain returned only an unrelated bacterial paper, so there is no literature to resolve it.
open_questions: What PF28404 actually represents (its Pfam seed alignment and the proteins it covers) and whether the N-terminus is a real signal peptide.

rationale: The only domain is CFEM (PF05730) with RBT5-family similarity, a GPI-anchor keyword and heme/iron keywords, so the name Chitinase 3 is a mis-annotation: there is no GH18 domain and I reject the enzyme reading. In C. albicans the homologous CFEM proteins Rbt5 and Pga7 are GPI-anchored, cell-wall-embedded heme-binding proteins that transfer heme from haemoglobin across the wall, which makes a genuine cell-wall-anchored surface protein very likely here. It is a wall-anchored nutrient-acquisition protein rather than a flocculin/ALS-type adhesin, and the evidence is from an ortholog in another species.
open_questions: Does the Coccidioides protein bind heme in vitro, and is it released from the wall by HF-pyridine; also fix the Chitinase 3 name in the annotation.

rationale: Signal peptide with an EGF-like domain, Cys 0.08 and disulfide-bond keywords describes a disulfide-rich extracellular or ectodomain protein, but there is no GPI call and the C-terminal tail hydrophobicity is negative (-0.3) while a transmembrane helix is annotated, so if it is anchored at all it is membrane-anchored, not GPI-anchored. Low Ser/Thr for a 923 aa protein, no repeats and no O-glycosylated stalk rule out the mannoprotein/flocculin architecture. Whether the ectodomain reaches the wall is unknown, and no model called it.
open_questions: Topology determination (is the TM real and where) and whether the EGF-like repeats mediate any cell-cell or matrix binding.

rationale: 487 aa GH18 chitinase with a C-terminal hevein-type chitin-binding domain (IPR001579), signal peptide and no GPI signal (tail hydrophobicity 1.3): the Cts1/Cht3-type secreted chitinase. C. albicans Cht3 is secreted into the medium and is the principal chitinase activity; surface-shaving proteomics found chitinase-like proteins abundant on C. parapsilosis yeast cells but without locus assignment.
open_questions: none

rationale: YEL028W_C family (PF29692), an uncharacterized Saccharomycetaceae family predicted to be secreted; signal peptide present but the C-terminus (...LPARVLAKQVL) is not a GPI signal, the 150-aa body is Leu/Val-rich and ordered, and Ser/Thr is only 14 percent. No feature of a wall mannoprotein or adhesin.
open_questions: Characterization of S. cerevisiae YEL028W; secretome proteomics.

rationale: Two CBM1 fungal cellulose-binding modules in a 257 aa secreted protein with no catalytic domain describes a carbohydrate-binding protein, usually an appendage of a secreted cellulase, not a wall anchor. There is no GPI call, tail hydrophobicity is 0.1, the longest disordered run is 36 residues and Ser+Thr is 0.22, so none of the GPI-mannoprotein features are present. CBM1 binds cellulose and chitin, so a surface carbohydrate-binding role cannot be excluded, but calling it an adhesin would overreach; it is also not an enzyme, having no catalytic module.
open_questions: Does the protein bind chitin or glucan of the fungal wall rather than plant cellulose, and is it retained in the wall fraction?

rationale: Swiss-Prot annotates this 67-aa ORF as a probable pseudogene product, a fragmentary flocculin piece similar to FLO1 in the subtelomeric FLO cluster; it has a signal-peptide-like N-terminus but no stalk, no PA14 domain and no GPI tail (...ASNWN), so it cannot be a wall-anchored adhesin even if translated. The flocculin family similarity reflects its origin, not a function. The ER GO term is high-throughput data.
open_questions: Ribosome profiling or proteomic evidence of translation; nothing else would make it a wall protein.
